spelling_fixes.StartLocation: Abu Sultan–Ain Sokhna gas line tie-in (Sokhna–Cairo Rd / Wadi Hagul Rd junction)

sheet_conflicts: Sheet StartLocation/EndLocation were blank (nothing contradicted), but flag a real risk of conflation: a SEPARATE sibling project, 'New Capital–Dahshur (Siemens)' (32in, 70km, 605M EGP, presidency.eg-confirmed), ALSO feeds the same NAC power station but via a different corridor (from the Dahshur compressor-station direction, south/southwest of Cairo). This 63km/327M-EGP line (P7574) instead taps the Abu Sultan–Ain Sokhna line east of Cairo, near Ain Sokhna. Do not merge the two corridors if GEM tracks the Dahshur line under another PID.
notes: Strong resolution: the Egyptian Presidency's own project registry has a page specifically for this line ('إنشاء خط غاز لمحطة كهرباء العاصمة الإدارية الجديدة (سيمينز)') giving 32in/63km/327M EGP — an EXACT match to the sheet's 63.0km. elbalad.news (2016), reporting the Official Gazette land-appropriation decree, independently gives the detailed route (65km, matching within measurement tolerance) and the two chamber locations. petro-news.com's 2020s project-list article corroborates the same 63km/327M-EGP figures (likely itself sourced from the presidency registry, so treat as reinforcing rather than fully independent). Overall: 2 reasonably independent sources (official registry + contemporaneous press) on the pipeline's existence/length/cost, but the START coordinate is only as precise as 'the named road junction' — recommend RouteAccuracy='low' (rung-4 great-circle only).

end.name: New Administrative Capital (power-station gas feed / national-grid tap)
end.coord_basis: Arabic Wikipedia infobox coordinate for the NAC power station (same anchor used for P7574): 29°54'29"N 31°45'18"E

sheet_conflicts: The presidency.eg source describes the FULL corridor as a single 42in/165km project across Cairo, Ismailia, AND Port Said governorates, serving MULTIPLE purposes (national-grid reinforcement, NAC power-station feed, plus supply to south-Cairo areas and Upper Egypt consumers) — not a simple point-to-point Abu Sultan→NAC line. This GEM PID's own segment label ('Abu Sultan–New Administrative Capital segment', 73km) appears to isolate only the Abu Sultan→NAC portion of that larger 165km project; the El Tina→Abu Sultan portion (~92km implied) is presumably a separate GEM PID not in this batch — worth confirming there is no length double-count across PIDs for the same physical trunk, and that 'El Tina' (in this PID's pipeline_name) isn't mistakenly implying this 73km segment starts at El Tina rather than Abu Sultan. Also: 'New Administrative Capital' here may be a grid tap/metering point rather than literally the Siemens plant gate — treat the NAC coordinate as the named destination hub, not a confirmed exact physical terminus.
notes: Resolved via the same presidency.eg national-projects registry (dated July 2019) that separately covers P7574, corroborated by petro-news.com's project-list summary (same 42in/165km/3.335B-EGP figures). Confidence: moderate — solid on the project's existence, corridor, and total length, but the SPECIFIC 73km sub-segment's own start/end are inferred from the sheet's segment label rather than independently measured in the source. Abu Sultan is confirmed as a real, named gas-grid station (also the tie-in point for P7574's separate line), consistent with the hint that it sits on the Great Bitter Lake side near Ismailia.

Could not source a specific named public project matching 'Cairo Ring–Port Said Gas Pipeline' (130km) despite an extensive search: the Ministry of Petroleum's official 'national gas grid lines' PDF (2020, https://www.petroleum.gov.eg/ar-eg/gas-and-petrol/distribution-marketing-transporting/Documents/2020خطوط_الشبكة_القومية_للغازات_الطبيعية.pdf) is prose-only and names no line-by-line projects; a trade-press '39 projects' list (petro-news.com/95212/) and a '16,000km' list (youm7.com) both enumerate ~9 named national gas trunks built 2014-2023 with none matching this name/length; GASCO's own site (gasco.com.eg/gas-grid) gives only grid-wide totals, not a project list; multiple Arabic-language searches for 'الحلقي'/'الدائري' (ring) + بورسعيد, and for an Ismailia–Port Said line, returned only adjacent-but-distinct projects: 'Duplication of the Gamal–Damietta gas line' (42in, 50km, Damietta/Port Said governorates, presidency.eg) and 'Development of the West Port Said gas-processing station' (presidency.eg) — neither matches this PID's length or the 'Cairo Ring' descriptor. Best working hypothesis (UNVERIFIED): a segment of a Cairo-area gas ring-main / distribution hub extended east toward Port Said, plausibly related to or overlapping the same corridor as the El Tina–Abu Sultan–NAC trunk (P8002) which itself crosses Port Said governorate — but no source ties this specific 130km figure or a 'Cairo Ring' name to a documented project. Recommend a follow-up pass once WebSearch quota resets, or checking GASCO/EGAS's internal project archive directly; leaving as ROUTE_PARTIAL (corridor-only, no endpoints) rather than guessing coordinates.

start.name: El Kureimat power station complex
start.coord_basis: OSM/Nominatim geocode of 'قرية الكريمات' (Kureimat village), Giza Governorate — nearest named place to the power complex; the plant's own gate coordinate is not published.

end.name: Al Tebbin (El Tebbin) thermal power station
end.coord_basis: OSM/Nominatim geocode of 'محطة كهرباء التبين' (Tebbin power station), an industrial-landuse polygon in Helwan, Cairo Governorate.

notes: Both endpoint FACILITIES are independently, publicly confirmed via official EEHC-subsidiary pages: Kureimat station (ueepc.com — Upper Egypt Electricity Production Co.: Giza Governorate, Atfih district, ~95km from Cairo, gas/mazout-fired, matches the hint's ~29.2N/31.23E) and Tebbin station (cairoepc.com — Cairo Electricity Production Co.: on the Nile Corniche, Tebbin district, Cairo, 700MW, gas/mazout-fired). HOWEVER, no public source found in this pass documents the SPECIFIC 87km GAS PIPELINE connecting them — the only 'Kureimat–Tebbin' line found in search was a same-named ELECTRICITY transmission line (almalnews.com, on a 2016 repair-cost story; a Ministerial Decree 75/2016 also references it), which is a power line, not gas, and must not be conflated. Marking resolved:false per the 'source the pipeline claim, not just the place' requirement, despite having good coordinates for both plausible endpoints — these are offered as a strong lead for a follow-up search pass (try GASCO/EGAS project archives, or Arabic press once WebSearch quota resets), not as a sourced pipeline route.

notes: Kureimat endpoint is well-sourced (see P8021 notes); Zaafarana's location is confirmed by public geocoding but I found NO public source describing a gas pipeline export FROM Zaafarana to Kureimat specifically — the only Zaafarana gas-pipeline hits were unrelated: a short GEMPETCO offshore-to-onshore field pipeline at Zaafarana (elmostqpalelyuom.com/34335, ~18km, 4in — a different, much smaller project, do not conflate) and a PMS efficiency project (nabd.com) on the same offshore field. Notable lead: a real, named, mapped road — 'طريق الزعفرانة - الكريمات' (Zaafarana–Kureimat Road, per Wikimapia listings) — runs exactly this Gulf-of-Suez-to-Nile-Valley corridor across the Eastern Desert, ~89km from Suez per one Wikimapia entry (consistent with, though shorter than, the sheet's 163km total, which would include the Nile-valley leg down to Kureimat). Egyptian gas trunks are frequently laid parallel to such roads (as independently confirmed for P7574's Sokhna–Cairo Road corridor), so this is a plausible corridor, but NOT a sourced pipeline claim — marking resolved:false rather than guessing. Recommend flagging for a follow-up search once WebSearch quota resets (try GASCO route maps or Arabic press specifically on this corridor).
